ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: (2018·Changde mock exam) There exists an electric field in a certain region of space. The situation in which the electric potential at each point on the x-axis changes with position is shown in the figure. Between −x1 and x1 is a curve, and it is symmetric about the vertical axis; the remaining parts are all straight lines, also symmetric about the vertical axis. Which of the following statements about this electric field is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The electric potential energy of a positively charged particle at point x1 is equal to its electric potential energy at point −x1.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There exists an electric field in a certain region of space. The situation in which the electric potential at each point on the x-axis changes with position is shown in the figure. Between -x1 and x1 is a curve, and it is symmetric about the vertical axis; the remaining parts are all straight lines, also symmetric about the vertical axis. According to the figure, what is the relationship between the electric potential energies of a positively charged particle at point x1 and point -x1?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The electric potential energy of a positively charged particle at point x1 is equal to its electric potential energy at point −x1.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is the electric potential φ, and the horizontal axis is x. The graph of electric potential versus x is symmetric about the vertical axis; between -x1 and x1 is a curve opening upward, and the heights at corresponding positions on the left and right sides are the same. The dashed lines in the figure also indicate that -x1 and x1 correspond to the same horizontal height, so it can be read that φ(-x1)=φ(x1). Then reason: the electric potential energy of a charged particle satisfies Ep=qφ. For the same positively charged particle, the charge q is unchanged, and q>0; since the electric potentials at the two points x1 and -x1 are equal, qφ(x1)=qφ(-x1), so Ep(x1)=Ep(-x1).
